extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners handling nonprovisional international (Hague) design applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination, form practice, and prosecution of nonprovisional international (Hague) design applications designating the United States, including requirements for reproductions, claims, notifications of refusal, inventor's oaths, restriction, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend Claim 'As Shown' (Form ¶ 15.62)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proper form (37 CFR 1.153 or 37 CFR 1.1025), the claim amended to read: "[I/We] claim: The ornamental design for [title of article] as shown."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, insert --must be-- or --has been--. In bracket 2, insert --I-- or --We--. In bracket 3, insert title of the article in which the design is embodied or applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend Claim 'As Shown and Described' (Form ¶ 15.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proper form (37 CFR 1.153 or 37 CFR 1.1025), the claim amended to read: "[I/We] claim: The ornamental design for [title of article] as shown and described."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, insert --must be-- or --has been--. In bracket 2, insert --I-- or --We--. In bracket 3, insert title of the article in which the design is embodied or applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of 'And Described' to Claim (Form ¶ 15.64)
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding "-- and described --" to the claim after "shown," indicate the reason and whether the wording "must be" or "has been" is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, insert reason. In bracket 2, insert --must be-- or --has been--.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions must be complete, clear, and comply with Hague Rule 9 / Part Four
rubrics_metrics.description: Every design application must include a reproduction (drawing or photograph) of the claimed design; the drawing or photograph constitutes the entire visual disclosure of the claim and must be a clear and complete depiction of the design applied to the article designated in the title, with nothing left to conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirements for reproductions for nonprovisional international design applications are set forth in Hague Agreement Rule 9 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions (see 37 CFR 1.1026). Drawing requirements in 37 CFR 1.84 do not apply except as provided (see 37 CFR 1.1061(b)). Reproductions must comply with Rule 9 and Part Four; amended reproductions submitted directly to the Office are subject to review under 37 CFR 1.1026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering conventions for international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When the same industrial design is represented from different angles, the numbering shall consist of two separate figures separated by a dot (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 for the first design, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 for the second design). Preserve figure numbering appearing in the published international registration during prosecution before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If designs are cancelled (e.g., due to restriction), applicants should not renumber the figures of remaining design(s). Any amendment to figures must comply with 37 CFR 1.1026 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions (see Section 405 regarding numbering). Use Form Paragraph 29.102 to remind applicants that renumbering is not required and to consider inventorship corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object to amended reproductions that fail to comply (Form ¶ 29.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 29.10 to object to amended reproductions received on [date] because [reason] for failing to comply with formal requirements (Rule 9 and Part Four / 37 CFR 1.1026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Insert the date amended reproductions were received and the reason for the objection (e.g., "the reproductions are not of a quality permitting all the details of the industrial design to be clearly distinguished" or "the reproductions contain explanatory text or legends"). Follow this form paragraph with form paragraph 15.05.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object and require consistency where views are inconsistent
rubrics_metrics.description: When inconsistencies are found among the views, the examiner should object to the reproductions and request that the views be made consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to Hague Agreement Rule 9(4), a Contracting Party may refuse effects of the international registration if reproductions are not sufficient to fully disclose the industrial design. When inconsistencies are of such magnitude that the overall appearance is unclear, the claim should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) as nonenabling and indefinite (see MPEP § 1504.04, subsection I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not object to reproductions already reviewed by the International Bureau on same formal grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions published as part of the international registration have been reviewed by the International Bureau for compliance with Rule 9 and Part Four and should not be objected to by the examiner on such grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended reproductions submitted directly to the Office pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121 are not subject to review by the International Bureau and may be objected to under 37 CFR 1.1026 as to matters of form where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate matter not forming part of the design (Form ¶ 29.20 / Administrative Instruction 403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter such as environmental structure or portions of the 'article' shown in a reproduction but for which protection is not sought may be indicated by statement in the description and/or by means of dotted or broken lines or coloring in the reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 29.20 only in an international design application. Administrative Instruction 403 permits such matter to be indicated in the description and/or by coloring. See 37 CFR 1.1026 and Hague Administrative Instruction 403.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration required where United States is designated
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States must include the inventor's oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.1021(d); see §§ 1.63 and 1.64).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is notified in a notice of allowability that an oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63, or substitute statement under § 1.64, has not been filed, the applicant must file each required oath or declaration no later than the date the issue fee is paid to avoid abandonment. The International Bureau reviews and communicates the oath/declaration to the Office when the published international registration is sent pursuant to Hague Article 10(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of international design applications follows Title 35 and Chapter 16 practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall make an examination pursuant to Title 35 of an international design application designating the United States; all questions of substance and, unless otherwise required by the treaty and Regulations, procedures shall be determined as in the case of applications filed under chapter 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices set forth in MPEP §§ 1504.01–1504.06 (Statutory Subject Matter, Novelty, Nonobviousness, Considerations under 35 U.S.C. 112, Restriction, Double Patenting) are generally applicable to international design applications designating the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Refusal: timing and required contents (37 CFR 1.1063 / Hague Rule 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each international design application to be examined, the Office shall send to the International Bureau within 12 months from publication of the international registration a notification of refusal where it appears the applicant is not entitled to a patent; the notification shall contain or indicate: (1) number of the international registration; (2) grounds of refusal; (3) copy of a reproduction of the earlier industrial design and information where relevant; (4) which designs are affected; and (5) a time period for reply under §§ 1.134 and 1.136 where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 12-month period may be replaced by 12 months (rather than 6) for Contracting Parties that declare such under Hague Rule 18. The notification must be dated and signed by the Office. Grounds of refusal must reference essential provisions of law and include details if based on similarity with an earlier design (filing date/number, priority date, registration date/number, copy of reproduction, owner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and permissible grounds of refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds of refusal may be a rejection based on a condition for patentability under Title 35 (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 171, 102, 103, or 112), a restriction requirement, and/or an objection; grounds may also be based on applicant actions (e.g., cancellation of designs, abandonment, renunciation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections based on requirements relating to form or content provided in the Hague Agreement and Regulations are not prohibited by Article 12(1) where the International Bureau didn't verify compliance (e.g., amended drawings submitted directly to the Office that fail to comply with Rule 9). Include copies of references cited by the examiner with the notification of refusal (but not applicant's IDS-cited references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to Notification of Refusal must be filed directly with the USPTO and meet signature/filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply to a notification of refusal must be filed directly with the Office and not through the International Bureau; the requirements of § 1.111 shall apply to such a reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies must be signed either by a patent practitioner registered to practice before the USPTO or by the applicant. If the applicant is a juristic entity, the reply must be signed by a patent practitioner (see form paragraph 29.100 Reply Reminder). If no practitioner of record, examiners should include form paragraph 29.100 and may include language informing who may discuss merits with the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview representation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A telephonic or in-person interview may only be conducted with an attorney or agent registered to practice before the USPTO (registered practitioner) or with a pro se applicant (inventor not represented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment as applicant’s representative before the International Bureau pursuant to Rule 3 of the Common Regulations under the Hague Agreement does NOT entitle such representative to represent the applicant before the USPTO. A registered practitioner not of record may participate if authorized via Applicant Initiated Interview Request Form (PTOL-413A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one independent and distinct design may be claimed (37 CFR 1.1064)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one independent and distinct design may be claimed in a nonprovisional international design application; U.S. law requires this practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one independent and distinct design is claimed, the examiner shall in the notification of refusal or other Office action require the applicant to elect one design for prosecution on the merits; requirement normally made before action on the merits but may be anytime before final action. Review under §§ 1.143 and 1.144.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction/election and follow-up guidance (Form ¶ 29.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a restriction/election requirement is made, inform applicant to consider cancelling drawing figures and description corresponding to non-elected groups and to correct inventorship as appropriate (37 CFR 1.48).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renumbering of drawing figures following cancellation of non-elected embodiments is not required; recommended to maintain consistency with published International Registration by not changing numbering. Any amendment to drawing figures should comply with 37 CFR 1.1026 and Part Four. Correcting inventorship after an Office action may require an additional fee under 37 CFR 1.48(c). If no practitioner of record, include form paragraph 29.100 Reply Reminder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications permitted to pursue protection for non-elected designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection for a non-elected design in a nonprovisional international design application may be pursued through filing a divisional application(s), either as a design application under 35 U.S.C. chapter 16 or as an international design application designating the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2920.05(e) for further information regarding divisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and description of broken/dotted lines or coloring to indicate non-protected matter (35 U.S.C. 112 considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using broken or dotted lines or coloring in a reproduction to indicate matter shown for which protection is not sought, applicants are encouraged to include an explanation of the purpose of the broken or dotted lines or coloring in the description to avoid uncertainty as to the scope of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged not to simply rely on a description to indicate matter not forming part of the design but to also identify the matter by broken/dotted lines or coloring. Presence of undescribed broken lines or color that renders the scope unclear may lead to rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b). Use form paragraphs such as 29.21 where undescribed broken lines or color render the scope unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for undescribed broken lines (Form ¶ 29.21) — 35 U.S.C. 112(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention as required in 35 U.S.C. 112(b) when reproductions include broken lines that are not described in the specification and the scope of the claimed design cannot be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 29.21 where presence of undescribed broken lines or coloring makes the claim indefinite; explain the figures and specify which broken lines are undescribed (insert figure references and specifics).
